title: A derived monoidal localization of a braided category is braided
statement:
Let $L:C\to D$ be a localization at a class $W$ containing identities [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property], with $C$ braided monoidal and $D$ equipped with its derived monoidal structure. More precisely, write $\otimes,\alpha$ for the tensor and associator of $C$, $\star,a$ for those of $D$ [def-sfb-monoidal-category], and assume that its binary comparison $q$ has the binary and ternary derived monoidal comparison data of [def-asd-derived-monoidal-comparison-data]. This includes that $a$ is the associator induced from $\alpha$, as in the canonical derived monoidal structure, rather than an independently chosen associator for the same tensor.

A braiding of $C$ means natural isomorphisms $\beta_{X,Y}:X\otimes Y\cong Y\otimes X$ satisfying both hexagon identities. Lift $q_{X,Y};L(\beta_{X,Y})$ and $q_{X,Y};L(\beta_{Y,X}^{-1})$ through the binary universal property, reindexing the two variables, to natural transformations $b,c:(-\star-)\Rightarrow(-\star-)^{\mathrm{flip}}$. Then $b_{U,V}$ and $c_{V,U}$ are mutually inverse. The resulting natural isomorphism $b_{U,V}:U\star V\cong V\star U$ satisfies both hexagon identities for $a$, so $D$ is braided monoidal. Composition $f;g$ means first $f$, then $g$.

proof.text:
Use $T(U,V)=U\star V$ and $R_l,R_r,q^l,q^r$ from [def-asd-derived-monoidal-comparison-data]. Reindexing its binary universal bijection by $(X,Y)\mapsto(Y,X)$ supplies the same bijection with target $T^{\mathrm{flip}}$ and counit $q_{Y,X}$. Indeed precomposition with this swap is its own inverse on both categories of tuples and natural transformations, and commutes with $L\times L$. Apply this bijection to the natural families $q_{X,Y};L\beta_{X,Y}$ and $q_{X,Y};L(\beta_{Y,X}^{-1})$. It gives natural $b,c:T\Rightarrow T^{\mathrm{flip}}$ with
$$b_{LX,LY};q_{Y,X}=q_{X,Y};L\beta_{X,Y},\qquad c_{LX,LY};q_{Y,X}=q_{X,Y};L(\beta_{Y,X}^{-1}).$$
This constructs actual transformations, with no assumption that $q$ is invertible.

source.place: Binary derived functor and descending constraints: existence of the two lifts; expanded abstract transport of lean/WeilConjectures/CategoryTheory/DerivedCategory/Monoidal/Braided.lean:250-305

proof.text:
For $X,Y\in C$, substitute the two factorization equations of step 1 to get
$$(b_{LX,LY};c_{LY,LX});q_{X,Y}=q_{X,Y};L\beta_{X,Y};L(\beta_{X,Y}^{-1})=q_{X,Y}.$$
Injectivity of the binary universal bijection in [def-asd-derived-monoidal-comparison-data], with test functor $T$, gives $b_{U,V};c_{V,U}=1_{U\star V}$. Likewise
$$(c_{LX,LY};b_{LY,LX});q_{X,Y}=q_{X,Y};L(\beta_{Y,X}^{-1});L\beta_{Y,X}=q_{X,Y},$$
so $c_{U,V};b_{V,U}=1_{U\star V}$. Swapping $U,V$ in this last equation gives $c_{V,U};b_{U,V}=1_{V\star U}$. Thus $c_{V,U}$ is the inverse of $b_{U,V}$. This uses inverses of the original braiding, not a symmetry assumption.

source.place: Binary derived functor and descending constraints: inverse equations; expanded abstract transport of lean/WeilConjectures/CategoryTheory/DerivedCategory/Monoidal/Braided.lean:250-305

proof.text:
The ternary universal properties of [def-asd-derived-monoidal-comparison-data] remain valid after any permutation of variables: given a test functor $V$, precompose $V$ and its proposed comparison transformation with the inverse permutation, apply the original bijection, and precompose the resulting lift with the permutation. These operations are inverse because the permutations commute with $L^3$. Consequently maps into $(U,V,Z)\mapsto V\star(Z\star U)$ are determined by their composites with $q^r_{Y,Z,X}$ on $L$-tuples, and maps into $(U,V,Z)\mapsto(Z\star U)\star V$ by their composites with $q^l_{Z,X,Y}$. Only injectivity is used below. The associator comparison also gives
$$a^{-1}_{LX,LY,LZ};q^l_{X,Y,Z}=q^r_{X,Y,Z};L(\alpha^{-1}_{X,Y,Z}),$$
by multiplying $a;q^r=q^l;L\alpha$ by the two inverse associators.

source.place: Ternary derived tensors and descended constraints: permuted extensionality and inverse associator equation; expanded abstract transport of lean/WeilConjectures/CategoryTheory/DerivedCategory/Monoidal/Braided.lean:250-305

proof.text:
Fix $X,Y,Z\in C$ and abbreviate $x=LX,y=LY,z=LZ$. Let $H=a_{x,y,z};b_{x,y\star z};a_{y,z,x}$ be the first forward hexagon path. Naturality of $b$ and its factorization equation, followed by the associator comparison from [def-asd-derived-monoidal-comparison-data], give
$$\begin{aligned}
H;q^r_{Y,Z,X}
&=a_{x,y,z};b_{x,y\star z};(q_{Y,Z}\star1_x);q_{Y\otimes Z,X};L\alpha_{Y,Z,X}\\
&=a_{x,y,z};(1_x\star q_{Y,Z});q_{X,Y\otimes Z};L\beta_{X,Y\otimes Z};L\alpha_{Y,Z,X}\\
&=q^l_{X,Y,Z};L(\alpha_{X,Y,Z};\beta_{X,Y\otimes Z};\alpha_{Y,Z,X}).
\end{aligned}$$
In the second equality use $b_{x,y\star z};(q_{Y,Z}\star1_x)=(1_x\star q_{Y,Z});b_{x,L(Y\otimes Z)}$, then the binary factorization with the pair $(X,Y\otimes Z)$.

source.place: Ternary derived tensors and coherence: first forward path; expanded abstract transport of lean/WeilConjectures/CategoryTheory/DerivedCategory/Monoidal/Braided.lean:250-305

proof.text:
For the other forward path $K=(b_{x,y}\star1_z);a_{y,x,z};(1_y\star b_{x,z})$, bifunctoriality and naturality of $q$ give
$$\begin{aligned}
K;q^r_{Y,Z,X}
&=(b_{x,y}\star1_z);a_{y,x,z};q^r_{Y,X,Z};L(1_Y\otimes\beta_{X,Z})\\
&=(b_{x,y}\star1_z);q^l_{Y,X,Z};L\alpha_{Y,X,Z};L(1_Y\otimes\beta_{X,Z})\\
&=q^l_{X,Y,Z};L((\beta_{X,Y}\otimes1_Z);\alpha_{Y,X,Z};(1_Y\otimes\beta_{X,Z})).
\end{aligned}$$
For the first equality combine $(1_y\star b_{x,z});(1_y\star q_{Z,X})=1_y\star(q_{X,Z};L\beta_{X,Z})$ and move $L\beta_{X,Z}$ through $q_{Y,-}$. For the last, combine $(b_{x,y}\star1_z);(q_{Y,X}\star1_z)=(q_{X,Y};L\beta_{X,Y})\star1_z$ and move $L\beta_{X,Y}$ through $q_{-,Z}$. The middle equality is precisely the associator equation of [def-asd-derived-monoidal-comparison-data].

source.place: Ternary derived tensors and coherence: second forward path; expanded abstract transport of lean/WeilConjectures/CategoryTheory/DerivedCategory/Monoidal/Braided.lean:250-305

proof.text: The forward hexagon for the assumed braiding of $C$ says that the two morphisms inside $L$ at the ends of steps 4 and 5 are equal. Hence $H;q^r_{Y,Z,X}=K;q^r_{Y,Z,X}$ for every $X,Y,Z$. Both paths are natural transformations, because tensor, $a$ and $b$ are natural. Apply the permuted ternary injectivity established in step 3 from [def-asd-derived-monoidal-comparison-data], with target $R_r(V,Z,U)$ and test functor $R_l(U,V,Z)$. It gives $H=K$ on all of $D^3$. This proves the forward hexagon without cancelling any component of $q$.

source.place: Ternary derived tensors and coherence: forward hexagon by injectivity; expanded abstract transport of lean/WeilConjectures/CategoryTheory/DerivedCategory/Monoidal/Braided.lean:250-305

proof.text:
For the first reverse path $H'=a^{-1}_{x,y,z};b_{x\star y,z};a^{-1}_{z,x,y}$, the inverse associator equation and naturality of $b$ give
$$\begin{aligned}
H';q^l_{Z,X,Y}
&=a^{-1}_{x,y,z};b_{x\star y,z};(1_z\star q_{X,Y});q_{Z,X\otimes Y};L\alpha^{-1}_{Z,X,Y}\\
&=a^{-1}_{x,y,z};(q_{X,Y}\star1_z);q_{X\otimes Y,Z};L\beta_{X\otimes Y,Z};L\alpha^{-1}_{Z,X,Y}\\
&=q^r_{X,Y,Z};L(\alpha^{-1}_{X,Y,Z};\beta_{X\otimes Y,Z};\alpha^{-1}_{Z,X,Y}).
\end{aligned}$$
The second equality uses $b_{x\star y,z};(1_z\star q_{X,Y})=(q_{X,Y}\star1_z);b_{L(X\otimes Y),z}$, then the binary factorization. The final equality uses $a^{-1};q^l=q^r;L\alpha^{-1}$ from [def-asd-derived-monoidal-comparison-data] and step 3.

source.place: Ternary derived tensors and coherence: first reverse path; expanded abstract transport of lean/WeilConjectures/CategoryTheory/DerivedCategory/Monoidal/Braided.lean:250-305

proof.text:
For the other reverse path $K'=(1_x\star b_{y,z});a^{-1}_{x,z,y};(b_{x,z}\star1_y)$, the corresponding calculation is
$$\begin{aligned}
K';q^l_{Z,X,Y}
&=(1_x\star b_{y,z});a^{-1}_{x,z,y};q^l_{X,Z,Y};L(\beta_{X,Z}\otimes1_Y)\\
&=(1_x\star b_{y,z});q^r_{X,Z,Y};L\alpha^{-1}_{X,Z,Y};L(\beta_{X,Z}\otimes1_Y)\\
&=q^r_{X,Y,Z};L((1_X\otimes\beta_{Y,Z});\alpha^{-1}_{X,Z,Y};(\beta_{X,Z}\otimes1_Y)).
\end{aligned}$$
In the first equality combine $(b_{x,z}\star1_y);(q_{Z,X}\star1_y)=(q_{X,Z};L\beta_{X,Z})\star1_y$ and use naturality of $q_{-,Y}$. In the last combine $(1_x\star b_{y,z});(1_x\star q_{Z,Y})=1_x\star(q_{Y,Z};L\beta_{Y,Z})$ and use naturality of $q_{X,-}$. The middle equality is the inverse associator equation of [def-asd-derived-monoidal-comparison-data].

source.place: Ternary derived tensors and coherence: second reverse path; expanded abstract transport of lean/WeilConjectures/CategoryTheory/DerivedCategory/Monoidal/Braided.lean:250-305

proof.text: The reverse hexagon in $C$ equates the expressions inside $L$ in steps 7 and 8. Thus the natural reverse paths satisfy $H';q^l_{Z,X,Y}=K';q^l_{Z,X,Y}$ on every $L$-tuple. Apply step 3's permuted ternary injectivity from [def-asd-derived-monoidal-comparison-data] with target $R_l(Z,U,V)$ and test functor $R_r(U,V,Z)$ to obtain $H'=K'$ everywhere. Together with naturality and the two inverse identities of step 2, these are exactly the data and axioms of a braiding on the given monoidal category $D$.

The worker's STATEMENT-DISPUTED repair is correct. On Z/2-graded spaces, twisting the associator by (-1)^{ijk} still satisfies the pentagon (both sides expand to ijk+ijl+ikl+jkl), but the forward hexagon at (1,1,1) gives +1 against -1, so the binary-only reading is false. The repaired item assumes the binary and ternary right-Kan universal properties and the associator equation a;q^r=q^l;Lα. These match the Lean exactly: the Kan property runs in the IsLeftDerivedFunctor direction, and q^l/q^r are counit12/counit23. The Lean instance satisfies every hypothesis, so this is not a weakening, and the item is not a target. I recomputed all 9 steps. The lifts b,c come from the swapped universal property, and the inverse identities hold without assuming a symmetry. Permuted ternary injectivity holds. Forward paths 4 and 5 reduce to q^l;L(α;β_{X,Y⊗Z};α) and q^l;L((β⊗1);α;(1⊗β)), reverse paths 7 and 8 to q^r;L(α^{-1};β_{X⊗Y,Z};α^{-1}) and q^r;L((1⊗β);α^{-1};(β⊗1)). The hexagons of C plus injectivity then give the hexagons of D. Each elementary mark is justified. The new node is statement-only and self-contained, with no existence claim and no restated clause of the item. Its searches were run, and no duplicate exists: I checked lem-sfb-multivariable-derived-calculus, lem-sfb-braided-monoidal-localization, lem-sfb-derived-monoidal, def-sfb-left-derived-functor, def-sfb-ringed-derived-comparison-data and lem-asd-derived-category-braided.
